title: Fix Rerun 2D image hierarchy and RGB projection colors
objective: Repair the programmatic flashlight Rerun stream so 2D image views do not rotate with the world/camera, the image streams do not look like segmentation maps, and the camera RGB projection is not black.
instructions: Move all regular 2D image inspection streams completely outside the spatial spear tree. Use a top-level non-spatial namespace such as images/rgb, images/depth_meters, images/world_normal_visualization, and images/diffuse_color_visualization, not spear/images/...
Keep only spatial/world entities under spear: spear camera pose/frustum, camera trajectory, camera position, and light direction/status if appropriate.
Keep projected RGB under spear/camera only if it renders as a camera image plane; it must use the same corrected natural RGB image as the 2D RGB stream.

Fix RGB color handling so final_tone_curve_hdr does not look like segmentation colors and the projected camera image is not black. Treat alpha carefully: if the source has 4 channels, output opaque RGB/RGBA as appropriate and do not let a zero/invalid alpha make the projection black/transparent.
If using rr.Image for the projected image, prefer a 3-channel RGB uint8/float image to avoid alpha issues unless the source alpha is known valid.

Keep depth out of spear/camera so it does not create a point cloud. For top-level depth, if rr.DepthImage still appears spatial or confusing, log a 2D depth visualization image instead or in addition, but do not put it under spear/camera.
Update README and running guide to document the corrected top-level image paths and spatial spear paths.
constraints: Do not remove the programmatic light control feature.
Do not run live simulator-dependent commands.
expected_outputs: Patched script and docs with non-spatial top-level image paths and corrected RGB/projection handling.
definition_of_done: Static check confirms no regular image path starts with spear/images and no depth image is logged under spear/camera.
ResultPacket states exact paths for 2D images, camera/frustum/projection, trajectory, and status.
